title: Deployment Lens: Cohort Contrast & Trace Linking for Rollouts
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Current Console rollout views show aggregate route-level metrics and basic cohort deltas but lack an integrated way to: 1) compare statistical differences across cohorts (canary vs baseline) for multiple signal types, 2) link individual cohort deltas to request traces, and 3) simulate auto-rollback impact before enabling policies. Goal: Build a Deployment Lens feature that surfaces cohort-level contrast scores, per-route token-cost and latency deltas, trace-linking from cohort diff rows into distributed traces, and an offline rollback-simulation sandbox. This will reduce time-to-detect regressions during canary/A-B/shadow experiments and make rollouts safer for customers with high SLAs.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Console displays a Cohort Contrast panel for a rollout with at least 6 signal types (latency p50/p90/p99, error rate, token-cost per request, top-1 output divergence, hallucination-rate estimate), 2) Each cohort row includes a statistically annotated delta (e.g., +12% p90, p<0.01) with a confidence band, 3) Clicking a delta opens a linked trace list pre-filtered for requests contributing to the delta and allows opening the full trace in our tracing UI, 4) A Rollback Simulation tab allows operators to preview the traffic, cost, and error-rate impact of an automated rollback policy for the selected rollout, 5) Feature has end-to-end tests and e2e dashboard in staging, 6) Performance: Cohort Contrast computes deltas for 1M requests across cohorts within 90s for typical queries, 7) UX reviewed and signed off by Design, 8) Documentation and runbook published.
engineering_notes: - Backend: new telemetry aggregation microservice (ENG-5021) to precompute cohort histograms and bootstrap CIs; uses bucketing approach to keep compute bounded. - Tracing: add trace sampling markers for rollout cohort tags and add API to fetch traces by cohort-filter (ENG-5022). - Console: React panel with D3-driven spark/delta visuals, and a Rollback Simulation sandbox that executes a synthetic re-play on a sample of recent requests. - Data: ensure KV cache keys for rollout cohorts are respected when constructing per-route cost deltas. - Risk: computing significance across many signals increases false positives; we'll use Holm-Bonferroni FWER correction. - Performance target: 90s compute for 1M requests; will add progressive streaming of results to the UI while aggregation runs.
rollout_plan: 1) Spike + prototype (2 weeks): proof-of-concept cohort aggregator and simple delta table (ENG-5021), 2) Design polish + trace linking (1 week): add pre-filtered trace list and open-in-tracing functionality (ENG-5022, DES-214), 3) Simulation + safety hooks (1 week): rollback simulator and permissions check, 4) Staging e2e tests + perf tuning (1 week), 5) Gradual release behind kill-switch to 10% of customers then 100% over 2 weeks. Target GA: console-2026.03.
testing_plan: - Unit tests for statistical aggregator and FWER correction. - Integration tests to validate trace-linking from cohort deltas to trace store. - Load test to validate 90s SLA on 1M request aggregation (k6/locust job). - Staging run with recorded canary traffic (shadowed) and manual validation by oncall. - Chaos test: simulate partial telemetry loss and ensure UI degrades gracefully. - Security review for data slicing to avoid exposing PII in sample traces.
mockups_and_docs: Figma mockups: https://figma.redwood.ai/file/xyz-deployment-lens | Spec doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Deployment+Lens+Spec | Runbook draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Rollout+Lens+Runbook
risks_and_mitigations: - Risk: high compute cost for large cohorts -> Mitigation: progressive aggregation, sample-first mode, precomputed daily histograms. - Risk: noisy signal leading to incorrect rollbacks -> Mitigation: multi-signal consensus and minimum sample size threshold before automated action. - Risk: exposing sensitive payloads in trace samples -> Mitigation: redaction pipeline and access control; only show traces to users with project-level trace permission.

notes: - This feature is aimed primarily at platform and enterprise customers that run automated rollouts with strict SLOs. - Consider later extension: golden-metrics pinning per-customer, adaptive alerting thresholds per route. - Coordinate with Security & Compliance for private deployment variants to ensure trace payload policies match on-prem defaults.
